newsitem.title: INDIA: India plans presidential decree on sugar exports.
newsitem.headline: India plans presidential decree on sugar exports.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Sunday proposed a presidential decree to free the export of sugar stocks, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
PTI quoted Deve Gowda as promising the special move to circumvent the parliament where his proposal was turned down by the upper house which demanded a closer study of the issue.
The prime minister was quoted as telling a public meeting in the eastern state of Bihar that a presidential ordinance would facilitate the export of 3.5 million tonnes of sugar stocks.
He said easier exports would "free sugarcane farmers from exploitation".
"In accordance with our policy, we have decided to soon promulgate an ordinance for the purpose so as to clear the arrears of the sugarcane-growers in various states in the country," Deve Gowda said.
On December 20, the Rajya Sabha, the parliament's upper house deferred approval of the bill seeking to end the monopoly of a private trading agency over sugar exports.
The bill was earlier approved by the lower house but needs the nod by the upper house before being submitted for presidential assent.
A presidential ordinance can only be issued when the parliament is not meeting. Parliament ended its winter session on Friday and is scheduled to reassemble only in February.

Indian sugar exports are currently channelled through the Indian Sugar and General Industries Export-Import Corp (ISGIEC), an agency set up by private millers. It is the only body permitted to export sugar.
The bill would permit private firms registered with the Agriculture an Processed Foods Export Development Association (APEDA) to export sugar.
